The guest known as Gnostic Informant returns to Danny Jones's podcast with a reading of the oldest Christian scriptures. His reading inverts the usual story. In his account, the god of those texts is really Satan, and the serpent of Eden told the truth. His framework comes from Gnosticism, the ancient movement that read Genesis backwards.

Jones follows the argument through the Nag Hammadi texts and the early church's war on the Gnostics who wrote them. Whether the reading is history or heresy depends entirely on the listener's premises, and the episode settles nothing. Its value is clarity about an old idea having a modern revival: that the creator of this world is its jailer. Few recordings state the Gnostic case this plainly for a popular audience, in the voice of its most tireless online advocate.

Professor Gad Saad brings his evolutionary lens to episode 1816 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Saad teaches marketing and studies how evolved instincts shape buying, mating, and belief. His book The Parasitic Mind argues that bad ideas spread like mental viruses.

Saad names the idea pathogens he says infect universities and media, from denial of biology to fear of offense. He defends free speech and science with wit and some heat. Rogan, a fellow critic of campus culture, gives him room to make the full case. Rational and bold listeners get the Gadfather in full form.
